scope: All HTML, CSS, JS, and data assets used by reports/ad_manipulation_report.html (v1 original), reports/adintel/adintel_dashboard.html (unified), and annotation_app/index.html (annotation studio).
self_contained_requirement: All three HTML files MUST remain fully self-contained — no CDN, no external scripts, no fetch/AJAX. They must work from file:// protocol.

libraries.purpose: Local vendored mini-D3 force-directed graph layout helper for the term-network visualization. NOT the real D3 library — a 89-line reimplementation that exposes window.d3LiteForce.layout(nodes, links, opts).
libraries.installed_version: d3-lite-force-local (no semver; vendored copy at reports/assets/d3-lite-force.js)
libraries.latest_verified_stable_version: n/a — this is a project-internal vendored helper, not a published package
official_documentation: Inline JSDoc comment in the file itself (lines 1-9)
release_notes_reviewed: n/a — no release history; file was created during the v1 dashboard build
security_notes: No known vulnerabilities. Pure mathematical layout code; no DOM manipulation, no network access, no eval.
libraries.upgrade_rationale: Not a published package. The real D3.js (v7) would add ~270KB and break the self-contained requirement unless vendored. The lite version is sufficient for the ~260-edge network in this corpus.
evidence: File reads at reports/assets/d3-lite-force.js confirm 89-line implementation
Original dashboard loads it via <script src='assets/d3-lite-force.js'></script>
Network visualization falls back to circular layout if this script is missing (confirmed in JS: window.d3LiteForce?.layout ? ... : circularFallback)
CRITICAL FINDING: the unified adintel_dashboard.html does NOT currently load this script — this is a regression that must be fixed

libraries.purpose: All interactivity in all three HTML files is vanilla JS: DOM manipulation via document.getElementById/insertAdjacentHTML, event listeners, inline SVG generation via string templates.
libraries.installed_version: ES2020+ (uses optional chaining, nullish coalescing, arrow functions, template literals, Set, Map)
libraries.source_location: Inline <script> blocks in each HTML file
security_notes: No eval() used. JSON.parse on embedded <script type='application/json'> blocks is safe (no script execution). All user-facing strings are escaped via esc() function.
libraries.upgrade_rationale: No framework to upgrade. Vanilla JS is the correct choice for a self-contained artifact.
evidence: grep for 'react|vue|angular|svelte|jquery' in all HTML files returns only CSS comment mentions ('Tailwind-inspired'), not actual imports
All three HTML files parse cleanly with no external script tags except assets/d3-lite-force.js

libraries.purpose: All charts (ROC curves, PR curves, heatmaps, corpus map scatter, term network, pipeline diagram) are hand-generated inline SVG strings. No Chart.js, Plotly, Recharts, or similar.
libraries.latest_verified_stable_version: SVG 1.1 (stable since 2003; SVG 2 is partial in browsers)
libraries.source_location: Inline <svg> elements generated by JS string templates
security_notes: SVG generated from escaped strings; no XSS risk because esc() escapes <>&"'
libraries.upgrade_rationale: Inline SVG is the correct choice for self-contained charts. A charting library would add 50-300KB and break the self-contained requirement.
evidence: All chart-rendering functions (lineChart, heatColor, renderTermNetwork, renderCorpusMap) return SVG strings

libraries.purpose: The council_candidate_inferences.json (611KB) is embedded directly in the HTML as a <script type='application/json' id='report-data'> block. This avoids fetch/XHR and makes the file work from file:// protocol.
libraries.source_location: Inline <script type='application/json'> blocks in reports/ad_manipulation_report.html and reports/adintel/adintel_dashboard.html
security_notes: <script type='application/json'> is NOT executed as JavaScript — it is inert data. Safe from XSS. The JSON is parsed via JSON.parse() at runtime.
libraries.upgrade_rationale: This is the standard pattern for self-contained data dashboards.
evidence: Original dashboard uses this pattern at line ~660: <script type='application/json' id='report-data'>
Unified dashboard replicates this pattern with three embedded JSON blocks (report-data, model-report, segment-report)

libraries.library: Inline CSS (no Tailwind CDN, no Bootstrap)
libraries.purpose: All styling is inline <style> blocks. The original dashboard's CSS comment says 'Tailwind-inspired utility report; no CDN required' — it uses utility-like class names but does NOT load Tailwind.
security_notes: No @import from external URLs. No url() references to external resources.
libraries.upgrade_rationale: Inline CSS is correct for self-contained. Tailwind CDN would break file:// support.
evidence: grep for 'cdn|@import|url(http' in all HTML files returns no external URL references
CSS uses :root custom properties (--ink, --muted, --paper, etc.) for theming

findings.finding: The unified adintel_dashboard.html does NOT load assets/d3-lite-force.js. The original ad_manipulation_report.html does load it. This means the term-network visualization in the unified dashboard falls back to a circular layout instead of using the force-directed layout.
findings.impact: Term network nodes are placed in a circle instead of a force-directed layout. This changes the analytical task: users can no longer visually identify clusters of co-occurring terms via spatial proximity.
findings.fix: Add <script src='../assets/d3-lite-force.js'></script> to the unified dashboard HTML before the main <script> block. Adjust the path relative to reports/adintel/.

findings.finding: The unified dashboard embeds three JSON blocks (report-data, model-report, segment-report) whereas the original embeds only one (report-data) and loads model-report/segment-report from inline JS variables. Both approaches work; the unified approach is cleaner.

upgrade_policy: No library upgrades are warranted. The dashboard is fully self-contained with zero external dependencies. Any change that introduces a CDN, external script, or fetch/XHR call is a hard fail against the self-contained requirement.
